cycle_title: Implement the Proposition L3.4 score screen in the GLM scaffold
completed: Added R/score_screen.R implementing the extra-parameter score screen of Proposition L3.4: it fits only the simple model and evaluates the complex model's score at the embedded simple fit, so no complex fit is required.
Enforced the nesting precondition with verify_nesting(), which raises rather than returning an uninterpretable statistic when the complex class does not contain the simple one.

Reported both a naive and a participant-clustered score statistic, because trials share a participant's latent parameters and the independent-observation variance is anticonservative; this makes the A-009 comparison-unit commitment visible in the output.

Added a per-block breakdown (linear ambiguity, nonlinear ambiguity, condition, colour cue) so the screen says which kind of false complexity absorbs residual structure rather than only whether some complex model can win.
Exposed the candidate-model formulas in R/fit_models.R so the screen and the fitted models cannot drift apart.
Wired the screen into run_replication(), summarise_model_selection(), a new R/run_score_screen.R sweep runner, a `make score-screen` target, and a CI step.

Added tests/testthat/test-score-screen.R with seven tests, including agreement between the score statistic and the likelihood-ratio statistic and a calibration check on data generated from the simple model.
Fixed a pre-existing bug in R/run_design_cell.R, which never sourced run_replication.R and so failed on every invocation of `make simulate-small`.
why_it_matters: The screen gives the simulation track a cheap, theorem-aligned way to ask whether a candidate false-complex parameterisation is even capable of strictly lower divergence, before any Stan or hierarchical Bayesian work is committed to it.

Running it on the current scaffold immediately found that the complex model adds a genuinely true term, which means the scaffold's existing complex-versus-simple comparisons do not isolate false complexity.
The block breakdown separates the genuinely false blocks from the true one, which is exactly the discrimination the theorem's boundary case 4 requires.

checks_run.notes: Regenerating responses from the simple model's own linear predictor over 200 replications gives a naive rejection rate of 0.060 against a nominal 0.05. The clustered statistic rejects at 0.020, conservative as expected with only 30 clusters.

decision_needed.question: The complex proxy M_K adds `ambiguous_value`, but the DGM sets sv_true = risky_value + theta * ambiguous_value, so that term is true rather than false complexity and the simple proxy M_S omits it. Should M_S be redefined to include `ambiguous_value` so the contrast isolates false complexity?
options: Yes, add `ambiguous_value` to M_S so that M_K's extra block contains only the genuinely false condition, colour, and nonlinear-ambiguity terms (recommended; it is what A-004 already assumes the contrast is).
No, keep M_S as it stands and redefine the scaffold's question as omitted-true-term recovery rather than false complexity, updating A-004 and C-005 accordingly.
Defer until the primary false-complex model is selected, since that standing PI gate fixes M_K and may change the extra block anyway.
decision_needed.default_if_no_response: Leave M_S unchanged and treat every existing complex-versus-simple selection rate in the scaffold as conflating true-term recovery with false complexity.

procedure_compliance.notes: No claim status was promoted; C-005 remains scaffold_only and C-004 remains planned. No new assumption was added: the screen consumes the already-proposed A-009 framing but adds nothing to the register. The definition of M_S was deliberately left unchanged because altering the model ladder is a PI decision, and the finding is raised as this cycle's decision gate instead. No restricted data, no expensive compute, no causal or literature claim.

risks_or_uncertainties: The screen implements a sufficient condition only. Failure to reject is not evidence that Delta ell = 0, and this asymmetry must not be read as a null result in any manuscript text.

Counter-example CE-1 of the L3 draft applies directly to the screen: a rejection is consistent with plain trial-level misspecification and no omitted context at all. The sweep confirms this empirically, since the screen already rejects above nominal at context_effect = none.

Under the current DGM and GLM proxy, screen rejection rates rise only from 0.125 at no context effect to 0.250 at a strong one, and the genuinely false condition block sits at the nominal 0.05 throughout. On this scaffold, omitted context is not producing detectable false-complex capability in the blocks A-004 designates as absorbers.
The clustered statistic is conservative with few participants; treat the naive and clustered statistics as a bracket rather than reading either as exact.
The screen is a GLM proxy result and inherits the scaffold_only status of C-005; it does not speak to LOOIC or Bayes factors, per Corollary L3.5.

The screen presupposes nesting, which is itself the open decision gate from the previous cycle. If M_K is redefined as non-nested, verify_nesting() will refuse and the screen will need a replacement built on a different sufficient condition.
next_bounded_task: Obtain the PI decision on whether `ambiguous_value` belongs in M_S, then re-run the sweep so the reported rejection rates isolate the genuinely false-complex blocks.
